h1: Appliance Removal Services in Caledon, Ontario — However Far Out You Are, We Come Get It

blocks.text: Appliance Removal Services in Caledon, Ontario — However Far Out You Are, We Come Get It

c: Out in Caledon, replacing an appliance is easy — it’s the goodbye that’s hard. Delivery crews will drop the new fridge but won’t touch the old one in the drive shed. There’s no curbside pickup on a concession road. And the transfer station is a tailgate-straining drive away. So we built the service the countryside actually needs: a fully insured crew that comes to your farmhouse, hamlet home or estate — however long the laneway — quotes flat and free at the door, and hauls the old machine to a proper recycling end.

blocks.text: Caledon East to Belfountain, Palgrave to Terra Cotta — Every Hamlet Is On Our Route

Caledon spreads its homes across some of the prettiest and least convenient geography in the GTA — century farmhouses outside Alton, horse properties near Palgrave, estate homes in the hills, village houses in Inglewood and Cheltenham. Live Junk Free serves all of it, and the 660+ five-star Google reviews behind our name include plenty that start with "they actually came out to us."

items.title: Distance is never a line item

blocks.text: Your price is set by truck volume — one machine, small load; a shed's worth, bigger load — and by nothing else. The forty minutes of gravel between your place and the nearest plaza is our cost of doing business in Caledon, not a surcharge on your invoice.

items.title: Quoted at the machine, wherever the machine lives

blocks.text: Kitchen, mudroom, barn, drive shed, the second basement under the addition — we quote after seeing the appliance and its route out, in person. That free look is why the flat number holds: no phone guesses, no adjusting later.

items.title: The whole job rides in one figure

blocks.text: Standard disconnection, dolly and strap work, floor protection, the long haul out and every recycling fee at the far end — one approved price covers all of it. Rusted feet, seized doors and awkward barn thresholds change nothing.

items.title: Country homes run country equipment — we haul that too

blocks.text: Rural Caledon appliances go beyond kitchen and laundry: drained well pressure tanks, retired water softeners and treatment systems, sump and utility pumps, old generators, and propane appliances (professionally disconnected first). If it served the property and it's done serving, it's on our list.

items.title: No pressure at the door — ever

blocks.text: The quote is free, carries no deposit, and doesn't expire when we drive off. Say yes and the machine leaves within minutes; say no and so do we, no charge; say "after harvest" and we'll see you then.

blocks.text: The national brands fold royalty fees into every pickup and often hesitate at rural addresses anyway. We're locally owned, we like the back roads, and Caledon pickups run 30–50% cheaper with us for the same result.

Frequently Asked Questions About Appliance Removal in Caledon, ON

items.q: Q: Do you charge extra for rural Caledon addresses?
a: A: Never — distance isn’t in our pricing model at all. Truck volume sets the figure, starting at $125 for small loads, and a farmhouse past Belfountain pays the same rate structure as a house in Bolton. The free at-the-door quote is flat and final.

items.q: Q: The freezer is in the barn and hasn't run in years. Will you still take it?
a: A: Happily. Dead, dirty, decades old — condition is irrelevant to the pickup and the price. Empty out any food and we’ll manage everything else, including the walk from the barn to the truck.

items.q: Q: Can you remove well pressure tanks, water softeners and treatment equipment?
a: A: Yes — rural utility equipment is a standing part of our Caledon service. Tanks should be drained and disconnected from the water system beforehand (your well or plumbing contractor typically handles that during replacement), and then we haul the old units away with everything else.

A: We remove them once a licensed technician has disconnected and capped the line — that part is a safety and code requirement, not ours to improvise. Mention propane when you book and we’ll sequence the pickup after your technician’s visit.

items.q: Q: The new fridge arrives Thursday and the delivery crew won't take the old one. Can you?
a: A: That’s one of our most common Caledon calls. Book us for Thursday afternoon — or any day around the delivery — and the old unit is gone before the new one has finished levelling. Same-day slots run seven days a week, 6AM to 11PM.
